response.original_title: Why are PLC charges applied by builders?
response.overview: Builders apply PLC charges (Preferential Location Charges) for properties that have a more desirable location or position within a real estate project. Some units may offer better views, more privacy, better natural light, improved ventilation, or easier access to open spaces and project facilities. For example, a park-facing, corner, pool-facing, road-facing, or higher-floor property may attract additional PLC charges. The main reason for PLC charges in real estate is that these preferred units are often considered more valuable than standard units. The PLC rate may vary depending on the location, floor, view, and other features of the property. Therefore, buyers should check the PLC in real estate, the applicable PLC rate, and the total PLC charges before making a purchase so they can understand the complete property cost.
